stories.headline: Google Plans Up to $40B Investment in Anthropic at $350B Valuation, With 5GW of Compute

key_facts.fact: Google is committing $10 billion now in cash at a $350 billion valuation, with another $30 billion to follow if Anthropic hits certain performance targets.
key_facts.excerpt: The Alphabet subsidiary is committing to invest $10 billion now, at a $350 billion valuation for Anthropic, with another $30 billion to follow if Anthropic hits certain performance targets.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud will provide 5 gigawatts of TPU-based compute capacity over the next five years, with room to scale further.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Cloud now providing a fresh 5 gigawatts of capacity over the next five years, with room to scale further.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's valuation stood at $350 billion in February; investors have since been eager to back the company at $800 billion or more. The company is reportedly considering an IPO as soon as October.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's valuation stood at $350 billion as recently as February; investors have since been eager to back the company at $800 billion or more, according to Bloomberg. The company is also reportedly considering an IPO as soon as October.

key_facts.fact: The deal expands a prior Anthropic-Google-Broadcom partnership for TPU-based compute that a Broadcom filing put at 3.5 gigawatts.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced a partnership with Google and chipmaker Broadcom, which designs custom AI chips for Google, to access multiple gigawatts of TPU-based computing capacity beginning in 2027; a subsequent Broadcom securities filing put that figure at 3.5 gigawatts.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic also recently secured $5 billion from Amazon, committing to spend $100 billion on AWS over 10 years, and struck a separate deal with CoreWeave for data center capacity.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic struck a deal with cloud computing provider CoreWeave for data center capacity. It also this week secured an additional $5 billion investment from Amazon, part of a broad agreement under which Anthropic is expected to spend up to $100 billion for around 5 gigawatts of compute capacity over time.

stories.headline: Meta Signs Multibillion-Dollar Deal for Tens of Millions of Amazon Graviton Cores for AI Inference

key_facts.fact: Meta signed a multibillion-dollar, multiyear deal to bring tens of millions of AWS Graviton CPU cores into its compute portfolio for AI inference workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has signed a deal to use millions of AWS Graviton chips to power its growing AI needs, Amazon announced Friday.

key_facts.fact: Graviton is an ARM-based CPU, not a GPU; agentic AI workloads like real-time reasoning, coding, and multi-step task coordination are driving demand for CPUs alongside GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: Note that the AWS Graviton is an ARM-based CPU, (a central processing unit, the chip that handles general computing tasks) not a GPU... Agents create compute-intensive workloads like real-time reasoning, writing code, search, and the coordination involved in managing agents through multi-step tasks.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's custom chip business is already generating $20 billion per year in revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon's custom chip business is already doing $20B/year in revenue.

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to spend $115B–$135B in capital expenditure in 2026, up from ~$72B last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta plans to spend $115B–$135B in capex in 2026 vs ~$72B last year.

key_facts.fact: The deal competes with GPU-focused chips; Anthropic already locked up Amazon's Trainium AI GPUs in a $100 billion, 10-year deal announced earlier this month.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic had already swooped in with a deal announced earlier this month that commandeered many of those chips for years to come. The Claude maker agreed to spend $100 billion over 10 years to run its workloads on AWS.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Project Deal Shows AI Agent Quality Creates Invisible Economic Inequality in Marketplaces

key_facts.fact: Anthropic ran a marketplace experiment with 69 employees where Claude agents bought, sold, and negotiated personal belongings; agents completed 186 deals worth over $4,000 total.
key_facts.excerpt: For one week, we created a classified marketplace for employees in our San Francisco office... our 69 agents struck 186 deals across over 500 listed items, for a total transaction value of just over $4,000.

key_facts.fact: In a secret parallel experiment, users with the frontier model Claude Opus 4.5 completed ~2 more deals on average than those with the smaller Claude Haiku 4.5.
key_facts.excerpt: users with Opus completed about two more deals than Haiku users, on average.

key_facts.fact: When the same item was sold by Opus instead of Haiku, it went for $3.64 more on average; Opus sellers extracted $2.68 more per item and Opus buyers paid $2.45 less.
key_facts.excerpt: When an item was sold by Opus instead of Haiku, it went for $3.64 more on average... Opus as a seller extracts $2.68 more on average for the same item, and as a buyer pays $2.45 less.

key_facts.fact: Users with worse-performing agents did not notice their disadvantage; perceived fairness scores were nearly identical (4.05 for Opus deals vs 4.06 for Haiku) on a 7-point scale.
key_facts.excerpt: perceived fairness was essentially identical for deals conducted by either model (4.05 for deals done by Opus agents and 4.06 for deals done by Haiku, on the same 1 to 7 scale).

key_facts.fact: Aggressive user instructions made no statistically significant difference on outcomes; what mattered was which model represented you, not how you told it to negotiate.
key_facts.excerpt: users who instructed their agents to act aggressively didn't have a better chance of selling items, didn't sell their items for more, and didn't pay less for what they bought.

key_facts.fact: 46% of participants said they would pay for a similar AI agent commerce service in the future.
key_facts.excerpt: when we asked them if they'd be willing to pay for an agent like this, 46% said yes.

stories.headline: Nvidia Closes at Record High, Pushing Market Cap Past $5 Trillion for First Time Since October

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares rose 4.3% to close at $208.27, a new all-time high, pushing its market cap past $5 trillion — only the second company in history to reach that mark.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock rose 4.3% to close at $208.27... Nvidia stock closes at record, pushing market cap past $5 trillion.

key_facts.fact: The rally was sparked by Intel's blowout earnings, which sent Intel shares up 24% — their best day since 1987 — and AMD up 14%.
key_facts.excerpt: Friday's rally was sparked by better-than-expected earnings late Thursday from chipmaker Intel... Intel shares spiked 24%, their best performance since 1987.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is up more than 14-fold since the end of 2022, driven by soaring demand for AI infrastructure from Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, OpenAI, and Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is up more than 14-fold since the end of 2022, driven by soaring demand for artificial intelligence services and models.

stories.headline: ComfyUI Raises $30M at $500M Valuation as Open-Source AI Media Tool Hits 4 Million Users

key_facts.fact: ComfyUI raised $30 million at a $500 million valuation, bringing total funding to $47 million. The round was led by Craft Ventures with Pace Capital, Chemistry, and TruArrow.
key_facts.excerpt: ComfyUI, a startup that helps creators control image, video, and audio outputs from diffusion models with a node-based workflow, has raised a $30 million funding round at a $500 million valuation. The round was led by Craft Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The open-source tool has over 4 million users and 60,000+ community-built nodes, with 150,000+ daily downloads.
key_facts.excerpt: That community is now: → 4 million users → 60,000+ community-built nodes → 150,000+ daily downloads

key_facts.fact: ComfyUI's node-based interface gives creators granular control over every step of image, video, and audio generation from diffusion models, unlike prompt-based tools.
key_facts.excerpt: their tool gained such significant traction among creative professionals... 'ComfyUI artist or engineer' listed as a job title on studio job boards.

key_facts.fact: Funding will go toward Comfy Cloud for enterprise, collaborative workflows, local experience improvements, and day-one support for new model releases.
key_facts.excerpt: → Comfy Cloud: for teams and studios that need security and scale → Collaborative workflows: versioning and iteration built for how studios actually work → A better local experience

stories.headline: Sam Altman Apologizes for Not Alerting Police About Mass Shooting Suspect's ChatGPT Activity

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman apologized to a Canadian town for not notifying police about a mass shooting suspect's troubling ChatGPT account activity when her account was suspended.
key_facts.excerpt: Sam Altman apologizes to a Canadian town for not alerting police to the activity of a mass shooting suspect when her ChatGPT account was suspended.

key_facts.fact: Altman said he was 'deeply sorry' and pledged closer work with governments to prevent future tragedies.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman has apologized to a Canadian town devastated by a February mass shooting, saying he was 'deeply sorry' the company did not notify police about the killer's troubling ChatGPT account.

key_facts.fact: The mass shooting occurred in February in Canada; OpenAI had suspended the suspect's account but did not report the activity to law enforcement.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI's Sam Altman apologizes to a Canadian town for not flagging a mass shooting suspect to police after a ChatGPT suspension — and pledges closer work with governments to prevent future tragedies.
